subject: hep-th
authors: Tea Martinic Bilac, Stjepan Meljanac, Salvatore Mignemi
abstract: It is well known that the algebra $o(2,4)$ generates the conformal group, but it can also be used to define some variants of the Yang model of noncommutative geometry on a curved spacetime. Starting from these examples, we construct a new physical model based on $o(2,4)$, that can be interpreted as a generalization of the Heisenberg algebra on phase space, with flat positions and momenta, but nontrivial commutation relations between positions and momenta and with the Planck constant promoted to an operator.
title_relatable: Can the conformal group algebra rewrite Heisenberg uncertainty?
hook: Physicists build a version of quantum mechanics where Planck's constant becomes an operator, using a hidden symmetry of spacetime.
summary: The conformal algebra o(2,4)—which describes how spacetime scales and rotates—can generate a modified Heisenberg algebra where position and momentum don't commute in the usual way and Planck's constant is promoted to a variable. This generalizes quantum mechanics on curved spacetime while keeping spatial and momentum coordinates flat, bridging noncommutative geometry and fundamental quantum relations.
